content.text:
Your design is right, and most of it is already in the code. Only one check stands in the way, and deleting it gives you your version with less code than the fix I wrote.

**What the code does today**

- Every saved reply records the format it was written in. The chat's history carries one `format` for the whole chat, and any reply written in a different format carries its own `output_format`. This is per reply, not per chat, and that's actually the better level: once a chat has switched, it holds replies in both formats, and a single field per chat couldn't describe that.
- The converter already runs on its own. When the Anthropic or OpenAI request builder meets a reply in the other format, it calls `assistant_output_as()` in `RecordConversion.cpp`, about 70 lines, and converts the reply's text and tool calls. Your messages and tool results are saved in a neutral form, so they need no conversion. Chats on a JusPrin account already rely on this, because the app's own turns there run on Expert, which can be served in a different format from the chat's model.
- The only thing that blocked your chat is the check in `AgentHost::begin_stream`. It fails the turn whenever a chat on your own API key meets a model in the other format. It was written before the converter existed and never got loosened.

**What I propose**

Delete that check, and drop the two helpers I added this morning, so the code is smaller than it was. The tests change with it. The test that expects a chat to refuse a model in the other format would instead expect the reply to go out, with the earlier history converted. I'd also extend the new test with a switch back to the first format to show the conversion works both ways. This also covers a future mid-chat vendor switch with no further work. Your rule that a chat can't change model mid-chat for now would still hold, because the composer greys out the picker after your first message. The UI would be the only thing enforcing that rule, not the host.

**Where your design costs something**

- Conversion loses the model's reasoning. The converter keeps text and tool calls but drops thinking and reasoning blocks, because each provider signs those for itself. After a switch, the new model sees what the old one said and did, but not why. In practice that's usually fine.
- The first message after a switch costs full price. The conversion gives the same bytes every time, so the provider's cache works again from the second message on. But the first request to the new provider sends the whole history uncached. On a long chat paid in credits, that one message is noticeably more expensive.
- A third format would need more converters. Today there are two formats, converted pairwise. If a third arrives, such as Gemini's, pairwise conversion grows quickly. At that point a neutral format to convert through would be better. It isn't worth building for two.
- The converter only knows text and tool calls. If a provider ever returns other kinds of content, such as built-in web search results, they'd be dropped silently. JusPrin doesn't use any today, but I haven't checked every reply type each provider can send.

**Decision needed**

Removing the check changes one case beyond yours. You have a chat on Anthropic, then you delete your Anthropic key in settings. Today that chat fails with the same "kept in a form that model can't read" error. With the check gone, it quietly carries on with your default provider, OpenRouter, and the composer's picker shows OpenRouter's model. The other choice is to keep the error for this one case, which needs a small check that the chat's provider is still set up. Carrying on quietly costs nothing but could surprise you: the chat answers in a different voice. Keeping the error costs a few lines and leaves a chat you can't continue. My pick is to carry on, since the picker already shows which model is answering. Do you want chats on a removed key to carry on with the default provider, or keep failing?

**JusPrin Cloud:** you were right for chats that stay on the account: no key is involved, so they never hit this. There is one way an account chat can still lose its provider. You sign out of the account while you also have a key of your own set up, and the chat would quietly carry on with that key. That case now fails too.

**What changed** (in [AgentHost.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp)):
- **The format check is gone.** Your chat's case now works: the app's reply to the opened file was on OpenRouter, then you switched to Claude and sent a message. Switching back and forth between formats also works, so a future mid-chat vendor switch needs no more work in the host.
- **Every chat records its model at your first message.** Before, only chats on the JusPrin account did this. Chats on your own keys need it too, so the app knows which provider the chat was on after a key is removed.
- **A chat whose provider is gone fails instead of switching quietly.** The person sees one of two messages:
  - "This chat ran on Anthropic, and no Anthropic API key is set up now. Add the key in the AI settings to continue it, or start a new chat."
  - "This chat ran on your JusPrin account. Sign in again to continue it, or start a new chat."
  
  Before your first message, the chat still takes whatever model the picker shows.

**Tests:**
- The test that repeats your steps (open a file, switch to Anthropic, send twice) failed before the change and passes now.
- The old test that expected a format switch to be refused now expects the switch to go through, there and back. It also checks that each request carries the whole saved history.
- New tests cover a removed key and a signed-out account. I didn't run those against the old code first.

**Not covered:**
- **Chats saved before this change** on your default provider without ever using the picker have no provider stored. If that provider's key is removed, they still carry on with the new default.
- **The greyed-out picker on such a failing chat** shows the default model, not the one the chat ran on.

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.
